what_this_file_is: The adjudication behind the 318 -> 396 refresh of data/constructive_ratchet.json. gate::constructive went RED on its first honest run (it was an ORPHAN from 2026-06-12 until 2026-08-25, so nothing had measured it in between) with +78 / -0. This file records which theorems appeared, why each is admissible under the shard's own predicate, and the MEASURED axiom closure behind that verdict. The baseline was NOT refreshed silently.
how_to_reproduce: MATHVERSE_DUMP_ACCEPTED_CLOSURE=<path> cargo run --locked --release -p clean-mathverse --bin mathverse_shard -- build-native <dir>  (the dump is off unless the variable is set; the default build path is unchanged). Closures come from Environment::axiom_deps and Environment::foundational_axiom_deps, which share ONE traversal (Environment::axiom_closure_all) with the classifier itself, so the evidence cannot drift from the gate by re-implementing the walk.

reaches_classical_choice.note: THE NAMING CAVEAT, MEASURED. ProofQuality::Constructive means 'transitive axiom closure contains no DOMAIN-specific axiom'. FOUNDATIONAL_AXIOMS includes Classical.choice, so a theorem resting on classical choice is labelled Constructive by this predicate. That is the repo's 'prove' rule (closure subseteq {propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, Eq builtins}), and it is WEAKER than constructive in the ordinary mathematical sense. Classical.em is the sharpest instance: it IS the law of excluded middle, derived from choice by Diaconescu, and it is in this shard. The classifier is not wrong about its own predicate; the word 'constructive' overstates it. ADJUDICATED 2026-08-25 (lane LOOSE) -- see `naming_decision` below; this note is no longer 'recorded, not fixed'.

naming_decision.verdict: (c) KEEP the name, RENAME what the artifacts and the gate SAY, and make the exception set a measured baseline field rather than a footnote.

options_considered.option: (a) narrow the predicate so Classical.choice disqualifies Constructive
options_considered.why: It is a policy change wearing a naming fix. Classical.choice is in FOUNDATIONAL_AXIOMS by deliberate decision, and CLAUDE.md's proof-soundness rule is STATED as 'closure subseteq FOUNDATIONAL_AXIOMS (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice, Eq built-ins)'. Narrowing puts ProofQuality in direct contradiction with the written rule and with data/axiom_audit.json's domain-axiom metric, and silently reclassifies every downstream count (SoundnessReport::constructive_theorems, the native shard's accept filter, the gamma-crown reports). There is also no variant to move the 2 theorems INTO: AxiomDependent carries a domain-axiom list they do not have. A change of that size needs an owner ruling on the foundation, not a gate lane.

1109 `ProofQuality::Constructive` sites across the workspace (1819 ProofQuality mentions), on a #[non_exhaustive] public kernel enum -- a mechanical edit of that size buys no new truth. The reader who is misled reads the NUMBER, in data/constructive_ratchet.json and in the gate's output line, not the variant name at the definition site.

options_considered.option: (c) keep the name and record the exact exception set
options_considered.why: Plain (c) is what this file already did, and it decays: a static footnote saying '2 of 396' cannot notice 2 becoming 40. So (c) is implemented as a GATE, not a sentence.

what_changed: data/constructive_ratchet.json gains `classical_choice_dependents` (the exact names) and a `metric` field that states the PREDICATE instead of the word.

scripts/check_constructive_ratchet.py measures that set on every run from MATHVERSE_DUMP_ACCEPTED_CLOSURE -- the same dump this review was adjudicated from -- cross-checks the dump's accepted set against the shard sidecar, and REDs on any movement. Unlike name drift, the exception set is NOT laundered by staging the ratchet file: only --update --notes can move it.
The gate's green line now reads 'N foundational-axiom-only theorems' and names the Classical.choice exceptions out loud.
The ProofQuality::Constructive doc comment in crates/clean-kernel/src/env/axiom_audit.rs said 'Genuinely proved'. It now states the predicate, names the overstatement, and points here.
scripts/test_constructive_ratchet.py gains arms 8-10 (exception set grows -> RED; refused even when staged; an ABSENT field is not an empty set).

falsified.how: Deleting ONLY the exception-set check from do_check turns exactly arms 8, 9 and 10 red and leaves the other 11 green. Prepending `return 0` to do_check turns all TEN do_check arms red and leaves the 4 update arms green -- the literal count the registry claims.
